title: Dose-based infusions: mg/h, units/h and micrograms/kg/min to mL/h
blurb: Convert a dose per hour, or a dose per kg per minute, into a pump rate in mL per hour using the bag's concentration.
question: A man weighing 80 kg is prescribed dobutamine 5 micrograms/kg/minute. The infusion contains 250 mg in 250 mL. At what rate should the infusion pump be set?

teach.body: Formal rule: concentration = amount in the bag ÷ bag volume; pump rate (mL per hour) = dose per hour ÷ concentration, with the dose and the concentration in the same unit. Plain English: work out how much drug each mL holds, then how many mL deliver the hourly dose. When the dose is per kg per minute, multiply by the weight and by 60 first. This is a stretch item.
teach.cite: FACTS sheet section 4 (dose-based and weight-based infusions)

teach.h: Worked example: Mr Lewis in a coronary care unit
teach.body: Gareth Lewis, 80 kg, is prescribed dobutamine 5 micrograms/kg/minute; the bag holds 250 mg in 250 mL. Dose: 5 × 80 = 400 micrograms/min; × 60 = 24,000 micrograms/h = 24 mg/h. Concentration: 250 ÷ 250 = 1 mg/mL. Rate = 24 ÷ 1 = 24 mL per hour. Sense-check: 24 mL per hour of a 1 mg/mL bag gives 24 mg each hour.

teach.text: Missing the minutes-to-hours step or the micrograms-to-mg step in a micrograms/kg/minute infusion. Forgetting × 60 makes the rate sixty times too slow; forgetting ÷ 1000 makes it a thousand times too fast. Write the unit beside every line of working.

teach.body: To check a running infusion, reverse it: dose per hour = rate × concentration. Heparin 25,000 units in 50 mL (500 units/mL) running at 1.6 mL per hour delivers 1.6 × 500 = 800 units per hour. Always take the concentration from the bag label in the question.

items: Concentration = amount in bag ÷ bag volume.
Rate (mL per hour) = dose per hour ÷ concentration.
Per kg per minute: × weight × 60, then match units.
Classic errors: missing × 60 or the micrograms/mg step.
Check: rate × concentration gives back the hourly dose.

summary: You can now turn dose-based prescriptions in mg/h, units/h, per kg per hour and micrograms/kg/min into a pump rate in mL per hour. You can also check a running infusion by working back to the dose it delivers.

A.q: A man is prescribed unfractionated heparin 1,200 units per hour by intravenous infusion. The syringe contains 25,000 units in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour? Write your answer to one decimal place.
A.why: Concentration = 25,000 ÷ 50 = 500 units/mL. Rate = 1,200 ÷ 500 = 2.4 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction (0.42 rounds to 0.4).
whyNot.1: This uses a 500 mL volume instead of the 50 mL syringe.
whyNot.2: This uses 250 units/mL, as if the syringe held 25,000 units in 100 mL.

A.q: A person is prescribed insulin 6 units per hour by intravenous infusion. The syringe contains insulin 50 units in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour?
A.why: Concentration = 50 ÷ 50 = 1 unit/mL. Rate = 6 ÷ 1 = 6 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This multiplies the dose by the volume.
whyNot.2: This adds a zero, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction.

A.q: A woman is prescribed furosemide 10 mg per hour by intravenous infusion. The syringe contains furosemide 250 mg in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour?
A.why: Concentration = 250 ÷ 50 = 5 mg/mL. Rate = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This multiplies the dose by the concentration.
whyNot.3: This uses a 500 mL volume instead of the 50 mL syringe.

B.q: A man weighing 80 kg is prescribed dobutamine 5 micrograms/kg/minute. The infusion contains 250 mg in 250 mL. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour?
B.why: 5 × 80 = 400 micrograms/min. × 60 = 24,000 micrograms/h = 24 mg/h. Concentration = 1 mg/mL. Rate = 24 ÷ 1 = 24 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This leaves out the × 60, giving a rate per minute.
whyNot.1: This leaves the dose in micrograms and divides by a concentration in mg.

B.q: A child weighing 18 kg is prescribed morphine 20 micrograms/kg/hour by intravenous infusion. The syringe contains morphine 18 mg in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour?
B.why: Dose = 20 × 18 = 360 micrograms/h = 0.36 mg/h. Concentration = 18 ÷ 50 = 0.36 mg/mL. Rate = 0.36 ÷ 0.36 = 1 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This leaves the dose in micrograms and divides by a concentration in mg.
whyNot.2: This divides by 10,000, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This divides by 100, a tenfold error.

B.q: A child weighing 42 kg is prescribed insulin 0.05 units/kg/hour by intravenous infusion. The syringe contains insulin 50 units in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour? Write your answer to one decimal place.
B.why: Dose = 0.05 × 42 = 2.1 units/h. Concentration = 1 unit/mL. Rate = 2.1 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This reads 0.05 as 0.5 units/kg/hour, a tenfold error.
whyNot.1: This leaves out the weight (0.05 rounds to 0.1).
whyNot.2: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction.

C.q: A woman weighing 75 kg is prescribed noradrenaline 0.1 micrograms/kg/minute. The syringe contains noradrenaline 4 mg in 50 mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour? Write your answer to one decimal place.
C.why: 0.1 × 75 = 7.5 micrograms/min. × 60 = 450 micrograms/h = 0.45 mg/h. Concentration = 4 ÷ 50 = 0.08 mg/mL. Rate = 0.45 ÷ 0.08 = 5.625, which is 5.6 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: This leaves out the × 60 (0.09 rounds to 0.1).
whyNot.2: This leaves the dose in micrograms and divides by a concentration in mg.
whyNot.3: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction.

C.q: A man is prescribed lidocaine 2 mg per minute by intravenous infusion. The bag contains lidocaine 1 g in 500 mL. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour?
C.why: Dose = 2 × 60 = 120 mg/h. Concentration = 1000 mg ÷ 500 = 2 mg/mL. Rate = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This leaves out the × 60, giving a rate per minute.
whyNot.1: This multiplies by the concentration instead of dividing.
whyNot.3: This leaves the bag in g and the dose in mg.

C.q: A syringe of heparin 25,000 units in 50 mL is running at 1.6 mL per hour. How many units of heparin per hour is the person receiving?

whyNot.0: This uses a 500 mL volume instead of the 50 mL syringe.
whyNot.2: This reads 1.6 mL as 16 mL, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This multiplies by the whole syringe amount, not the amount per mL.

reteach.title: How much is in each mL?
reteach.question: A syringe holds 250 mg in 50 mL and 10 mg per hour is prescribed. What rate?

blocks.body: 250 ÷ 50 = 5 mg in each mL. To give 10 mg each hour you need 10 ÷ 5 = 2 mL each hour.

blocks.text: Dividing the dose by the whole bag (10 ÷ 250) gives a fraction that ignores the volume the drug is in.

explain.body: Amount in the bag ÷ volume of the bag. 250 mg in 50 mL = 5 mg/mL.

test.q: A syringe contains 250 mg of a medicine in 50 mL. What is the concentration in mg per mL?

whyNot.1: This divides volume by amount, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This divides by 5 instead of 50, a tenfold error.

test.q: A medicine is prescribed at 3 micrograms per minute. How many micrograms is this per hour?

whyNot.0: This divides by 60 instead of multiplying.
whyNot.1: This multiplies by 600, a tenfold error.
whyNot.2: This multiplies by 6, a tenfold error the other way.

explain.body: micrograms/kg/min × kg × 60 = micrograms per hour. 5 × 60 kg × 60 = 18,000.

test.q: A person weighing 60 kg is prescribed a medicine at 5 micrograms/kg/minute. How many micrograms per hour is this?

whyNot.0: This is the dose per minute, not per hour.
whyNot.3: This divides by 60 instead of multiplying.

test.q: A person is prescribed a medicine at 6 mg per hour. The syringe contains 2 mg in each mL. At what rate should the syringe pump be set, in mL per hour?

whyNot.0: This multiplies the dose by the concentration.
whyNot.2: This divides the concentration by the dose, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This adds a zero, a tenfold error.
